answers.q1: It reads as one window being REPLACED by a different one, not a single surface resizing. Frames 001-004 show a full-width dark strip (red dot + 'Recording' label + timer + text buttons 'Notes/Captions/Ask Astra' + eye icon + red stop button). Between frame 004 and 005 that entire strip is gone and a much larger white card (a full meeting workspace with title, transcript panel, decision/action lists, chat input) appears, topped by a small floating black pill with a different, icon-only control set (dot, pause, comment, expand, ellipsis, stop). Because the control iconography, layout, width and position all change simultaneously with no visible intermediate state, it reads as a swap/materialization of a new window rather than the same surface growing.
answers.q2: Yes, a major layout shift occurs at 004→005: content jumps from a thin top strip to a large centered card with entirely different internal structure and position. Within the large-card frames (005-009) there is no further positional shift; only content values change in place (timer digits, and two placeholder lines being replaced by real items) without moving surrounding layout.
answers.q3: No flicker or half-drawn rendering is visible in any single frame, but the 006→007 transition shows two content blocks ('決まったこと' and 'やること') switching instantly from placeholder text ('...を待っています') to fully-formed items with avatar initial, speaker name, timestamp and a chevron — no partial/loading state is visible in between, so it reads as a pop-in rather than a rendered transition. The 004→005 jump is similarly instantaneous with no partial-size or partial-opacity intermediate frame captured.
answers.q4: Partially. The timer (00:00→00:01→00:02→00:03) and the recording dot give continuous feedback that recording is live. The appearance of transcript-derived items in 007 is understandable in context (the meeting produced a decision and an action item), but there is no visible transition/highlight marking them as newly added, so a viewer would only notice via careful before/after comparison. The 004→005 change itself (small bar to full workspace) has no visible causal cue in these frames — it just appears, so 'why now' isn't explained by the motion.
answers.q5: Mixed. The timer ticking and the incremental appearance of decision/action items do explain real state (recording duration, live meeting understanding) — that motion is purposeful. But the large structural jump at 004→005 does not itself explain anything visually; it looks like an instant swap rather than a motion that communicates 'the recording UI is expanding into a workspace.'
answers.q6: The 004→005 transition would feel abrupt if it truly happens within one 0.25s frame gap with no scaling/fade — going from a slim strip to a full multi-panel workspace instantly reads as jarring rather than smooth. The 006→007 item pop-in (placeholders replaced by real content with no fade/slide) would also feel abrupt. Two pairs of frames (001-002 and 003-004, 007-008) show zero change at all, suggesting dead time between the timer ticks with nothing else happening, which is fine but reinforces that the one real transition is comparatively sudden.

observations.what: Timer advances 00:00→00:01; layout and buttons unchanged.

Abrupt replacement: full-width dark recording strip (text buttons, eye icon) disappears; a large white meeting-workspace card appears with a small floating icon-only black pill at top. Size, position and control set all change at once with no visible intermediate frame.
Placeholder text under '決まったこと' and 'やること' is replaced by two concrete items (speaker initial, name, quote, timestamp, chevron) with no visible transition animation.

weaknesses.what: The switch from the compact recording strip to the full meeting workspace shows no shared visual anchor or morph — different icon set, different width/position — so it reads as a different window appearing rather than the same control surface growing.
weaknesses.fix: Keep the recording pill's visible identity (position, at least one persistent element like the red dot) constant through the transition and animate the workspace card growing from/around it so the eye can track it as one surface.

weaknesses.what: The 004→005 jump moves all content from a thin top strip to a large centered card in a single step with no captured intermediate size.
weaknesses.fix: Add an intermediate scaling/expansion frame (or slow the capture) so the size change reads as continuous growth rather than a jump cut.

weaknesses.what: Decision/action items pop in fully-formed between 006 and 007 with no entry animation, which can look like a jarring content swap rather than an update.
weaknesses.fix: Fade-in or slide-in newly added transcript-derived items so their appearance reads as an incremental update rather than an instant replacement of placeholder text.

weaknesses.what: The large structural transition (strip → workspace) carries no visible motion cue explaining cause, so it doesn't communicate why the UI expanded.
weaknesses.fix: Tie the expansion to a visible trigger animation (e.g., the strip visibly stretching/unfolding into the card) so the size change itself explains the state transition.
